 Advertisement General Motors issues recalls for more than 80,000 vehicles
 Advertisement Updated: 3:16 PM EST Nov 5, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Livia Daggett Digital Curator General Motors issues recalls for more than 80,000 vehicles
 Updated: 3:16 PM EST Nov 5, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Livia Daggett Digital Curator General Motors has issued two recalls, covering more than 80,000 vehicles.
 The first affects more than 67,000 Cadillac and Blazer vehicles. A software defect in the brake system control module may cause a loss of braking during “certain driving conditions,” the recall report says.
 Advertisement The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration report said that as of Oct. 29, GM was aware of 20 minor accidents associated with the Cadillac and Blazer vehicles. Two resulted in alleged minor injuries.
 GM described the driving conditions that could trigger the issue as follows: “When the brakes are lightly applied at low speeds during a sharp turn and the vehicle encounters a bump or depression – such as at the end of a driveway – a momentary release and reapplication of the brakes may cause the software’s slip calculation to misinterpret wheel movement. In some instances, this may result in a temporary loss of braking.”
 The second recall is for more than 12,000 Chevrolet Express and GMC Savana vehicles. That recall concerns a loose steering gear assembly nut. The company hasn’t heard of any crashes or injuries related to this recall, the report says, and it estimates that 1% of the vehicles recalled could have a loose nut.
 Hyundai recalls more than 94,000 vehicles over power seat fire risk Makes and models affected by the braking system recall, though not every vehicle is affected: 
 Cadillac Celestiqs from 2025-26
 Cadillac Lyriqs from 2023-27
 Cadillac Vistiqs from 2026-27
 Chevrolet Blazer EVs from 2024-27
 For vehicles that are capable of receiving software changes using wireless over-the-air (OTA) technology, owners who have accepted the relevant terms and conditions will be able to accept the software changes to resolve the issue via OTA without having to bring their vehicle to a dealership, the report said. However, all owners can have the updates performed at a GM dealer.
 Makes and models that may be affected by the loose nut: 
 Chevrolet Expresses from 2025-26
 GMC Savanas from 2025-26
 Dealers will check the steering gear serial number and replace the steering gear assembly if it's affected by the recall.
 Owners can reach out to GM’s customer service for more information on the recalls and next steps.
